title: Two Indicators at Same Reference Point

illustrates.quote: Transcribe each reference mark used at the same reference point as a separate indicator. Follow print order for these reference marks.

blocks.text: The semester was beginning with a flurry of activities. All the students were preoccupied with the details of the syllabus[ref:†][ref:‡] that was disseminated by the professor at the opening class.
blocks.features: Two reference marks (dagger, then double dagger) appear together, in that order, immediately after "syllabus", each keyed to its own note at the right.

blocks.text:
[ref:†]syllabus: the subject studied for a particular course
[ref:‡]syllabus: a summary outline of a course of study
blocks.features: Two short glossary-style notes stacked at the right margin, each repeating "syllabus" in italics with its own mark.

braille.notes: The dagger (@,?) and double dagger (@,]) are transcribed one immediately after the other, in print order, directly after "syllabus" -- two separate indicators at one reference point, per rule 16.7.2. Each note after the separation line repeats its own mark (with the italics indicator .1) before its own "syllabus" gloss.

resolution: illustrates.rule set to 16.7.2 per standards-map.md's own BANA §16/B004 §11 worked-examples table (the project's established canonical id), not either run's own guess. print.blocks/print.notes follow Run B's schema ([ref:MARK] tokens inline + a separate print.notes[] array of {ref, placement, text}), matching this task's required schema; Run A instead folded each note's real content directly into a sibling print.blocks entry with no [ref:MARK] markers and always an empty print.notes[] -- a schema-level difference, not a content disagreement. braille.width: Run A itself flagged this as weak evidence ("no line reaches exactly column 40, max observed is 39") before still recording 40; direct verification (lines 12618-12626, 9-space padding stripped) confirms no line reaches 40 (max 39, on four separate lines) and no page/line-number token anchors the right edge. Left null, per the same "never guess" convention applied to Examples 16-1..16-4 (overturning Run A, matching Run B). braille.lines: the two runs agreed byte-for-byte; kept as transcribed.
